newsitem.title: USA: Iomega plans slim Zip drive for notebooks.
newsitem.headline: Iomega plans slim Zip drive for notebooks.

text.p: Iomega Corp. said Wednesday it plans to develop a slimmer version of its internal Zip data storage drive for use in notebook computers.

The company said the new design will be 12.7 millimetres thick, allowing it to fit in most laptop computers and making the Zip, with its capacity to store 100 megabytes of data, a viable replacement for current 1.44 megabyte "floppy drives."
A megabyte represents roughly a million bytes of data.
Iomega already offers a 15 millimetre Zip drive for use in the expansion slot of laptop computers.
The new Zip drive will be a fixed, internal component and is expected to be available to laptop computer makers for use in their machines by the second half of 1997, the company said.
